Parallel Lines in a Cyclic Quadrilateral

GeometryCirclesTriangles
Game: This is a picture, not a game: when two lines cross inside the circle, the line joining the two new dots runs alongside AB.
How to play: Drag the dots A, B, C and D around the circle, or focus a dot and use the arrow keys. Tick the boxes to show the equal lengths, the two lines, the angle hints and the names.
Look for the math

Four dots on a circle, two lines crossing, and two new dots planted at just the right distances. Something surprising happens: the line through the new dots keeps the same direction as the line through the first two. Here is why, and where the surprise stops working.

What the picture builds

Points A, B, C and D lie on a circle. The two chords AC and BD meet at G. M sits on AC with AM = AD; N sits on BD with BN = BC. The page asks us to prove that, provided M and N are different points, MN || AB. The applet computes exactly these points: M is found by walking a distance AD from A toward C, and N by walking a distance BC from B toward D.

Two similar triangles

The inscribed angles CAD and CBD both subtend the same arc CD, so they are equal. Since G lies on AC and BD, this says angle GAD = angle CBG. The angles at G are vertical, so angle AGD = angle BGC. Triangles AGD and BGC are therefore similar, which gives the proportion AG / AD = BG / BC. Tick "Show hint" to see the four equal angles the proof uses.

One stretch, twice

Because AM = AD and BN = BC, the proportion becomes AG / AM = BG / BN. In other words, M is the image of A and N is the image of B under the same stretch about G. Writing k = AD / AG = BC / BG, the vectors satisfy M − G = (k − 1)(A − G) and N − G = (k − 1)(B − G). Subtracting gives M − N = (k − 1)(B − A): the two directions are the same, so MN || AB. When k = 1 the dots M and N both fall on G, and there is no line MN to speak of — that is why the page says "provided M and N are distinct".

What the checks found

The logic test compares the core with a second transcription of the applet's own method on all 331,776 quadruples of 24 positions around the circle plus 3,000 random ones, and checks the page's equalities on every crossing case: AM = AD, BN = BC, angle CAD = angle CBD, AG / AD = BG / BC, and MN parallel to AB all hold to about 1e-9 of the circle's radius. One remark on the page is wrong, though: it says the requirement that the chords cross is redundant. It is not. With the dots in the circular order A, C, B, D (for instance A at 30°, B at 210°, C at 150°, D at 300°), G lies on opposite sides of A and B along their chords, the similar-triangle step fails, and MN is not parallel to AB; the test measures a cross product about 2.83 times the radius squared. The port keeps the page's actual problem and the applet's construction, and reports this counterexample in the status line.

Tick "Show premise" and slowly drag C past the point where the chords stop crossing: the tick marks stay equal, but the two grey lines stop matching.
